examples.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
examples.problem: Find $\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)'$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048749/assets/9e23d542bfc56d506f5437a35a92c304d618109ef60086e1f5a7a4fee57d8a80.png) and $u(t) = t.$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)' = u'(t) \mathbf{g}(t) + u(t) \mathbf{g}'(t).
$$

Let's find $\mathbf g'(t)$ and $u'(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)g(t)+u(t){g}^{′}(t) \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+t\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -t \\ 2t{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -2t \\ (2t+1){e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Differentiate $2g(t)-h(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}g(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3t-3,\,-{t}^{2}⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-t,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and the sum rules, we have

$$
(2g(t)-h(t))^{′}=2{g}^{′}(t)-{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-2t⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}4⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2g(t)-h(t))^{′} & =2{g}^{′}(t)-{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =2⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-2t⟩-⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,6,\,-4t⟩-⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,6-(-1),\,-4t-0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,7,\,-4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
